neighbours.label: the speaker's own-claim slot: 'I' / 'You' / modal right after 'should' or an opening quote in a direct assertion or question ('why should I', '“You will')
fire: Which laptop should I buy if I mostly edit photos?
Why should I trust a company that hides its fees?
Don't reply with, “Well, I told you so,” when a friend is upset.
The teacher said, “You will not leave until the work is done.”
Honestly, I do not think that plan will work.
Where the road narrows, there should be a warning sign.
What should I say when my boss asks for a raise?
My father always said that “hard work pays off,” and he meant it.
quiet: Which laptop is best for someone who mostly edits photos?
Why would anyone trust a company that hides its fees?
Don't reply sarcastically when a friend is upset.
The teacher said the students could leave after the work was done.
Honestly, that plan probably will not work.
Where the road narrows, a warning sign is posted.
What is the best way to ask a boss for a raise?
My father always believed that hard work pays off, and he meant it.

notes: Card (+ pole, max 25.8): ' I'/'I' x10, ' "' x3, ' should', ' must', ' you', ' do' — 'why should[ I] avoid', 'said that[ "]all is number', 'stupid,[ I] thought', '“[You] will not'. Not probed. The - pole is need/insist (max 176), which suggests the + side is the speaker's own assertion vs. an imposed necessity; tested here only as the assertion slot.
